( 57 ) ABSTRACT
This disclosure provides methods , systems , compositions , and kits for the multiplexed detection of a plurality of analytes in a sample . In some examples , this disclosure provides methods , systems , compositions , and kits wherein multiple analytes may be detected in a single sample volume by acquiring a cumulative measurement or measurements of at least one quantifiable component of a signal . In some cases , additional components of a signal , or additional signals ( or components thereof ) are also quantified . Each signal or component of a signal may be used to construct a coding scheme which can then be used to determine the presence or absence of any analyte .

This example describes the simultaneous detection of up to three polynucleotides selected from dengue virus , HIV p17 , and HIV polyprotease . The coding scheme was as depicted in Table 11. As shown in Table 17 , each analyte was encoded as a single value of fluorescence intensity in a 20 single color . In this case , as described elsewhere in this disclosure , the coding scheme is non - degenerate by design . This is achieved by assigning an intensity value to each analyte that is equal to the cumulative intensity values for the prior analytes , plus one . Of course , as described else- 25 where in the specification , the initial assigned value can be greater than one , for example to better distinguish over noise . Similarly , the values assigned to each analyte can be greater than the cumulative intensity values for the prior analytes plus one , for example , to increase the separation 30 between the intensities and enable more simple assignment
of intensities .

What is claimed is :
1. A method of unambiguously detecting any unique 30
combination of presence or absence of at least five poly
nucleotide analytes in a plurality of droplets , the method
comprising :
( a ) providing a sample comprising , or potentially com
prising , at least one of said at least five polynucleotide 35
analytes ;
( b ) forming a mixture of said sample and at least five
hybridization probes , wherein each of said at least five
hybridization probes further comprises at least one
fluorophore and at most four fluorophores ; 40
( c ) partitioning said mixture into said plurality of droplets ;
( d ) exciting said at least one fluorophore to generate one
or more signals if one or more of said at least five
polynucleotide analytes is present in said plurality of
droplets , wherein said one or more signals comprise at 45
least one signal generated by excitement of said at least
one fluorophore ;
( e ) measuring said one or more signals to generate a
cumulative intensity measurement , wherein said cumu 50
lative intensity measurement corresponds to the pres
ence of a unique combination of presence or absence of
said at least five polynucleotide analytes in said sample ;
and
( f ) determining whether each of said least five polynucle- 55
otide analytes is present , in any unique combination of
presence or absence , based on said cumulative intensity
measurement ,
wherein the method does not require any step of
immobilization of said at least five polynucleotide 60
analytes or mass spectrometry .
2. The method of claim 1 , wherein each of said at least
five hybridization probes is complementary to one of said at
least five polynucleotide analytes .
3. The method of claim 1 , wherein said at least five 65
hybridization probes comprise one or more fluorophores
selected from one , two , three , or four fluorophores .
4. The method of claim 1 , wherein , in ( b ) , a droplet of said
plurality of droplets comprises said at least five hybridiza
tion probes .
5. The method of claim 1 , wherein , in ( b ) , a droplet of said
plurality of droplets comprises one or more of said at least
five polynucleotide analytes .
6. The method of claim 1 , wherein , in ( b ) , a droplet of said
plurality of droplets comprises at most one of said at least
five polynucleotide analytes .
7. The method of claim 1 , wherein said one or more
signals is generated during a polymerase chain reaction .
8. The method of claim 1 , wherein said at least five
polynucleotide analytes are at least seven polynucleotide
analytes .
9. The method of claim 1 , wherein said at least five
hybridization probes are at least seven hybridization probes .
10. The method of claim 1 , wherein said one or more of
said at least five polynucleotide analytes comprise cell - free
nucleic acid , tumor nucleic acid , fetal nucleic acid , viral
nucleic acid , or any combination thereof .
11. The method of claim 1 , wherein said sample is a
biological sample derived from a subject .
12. The method of claim 11 , wherein detecting the pres
ence or absence of said at least five polynucleotide analytes
indicates the presence of cancer or an infection with a
pathogen in said subject .
13. The method of claim 1 , further comprising transmit
ting information concerning the presence or absence of said
at least five polynucleotide analytes through a computer
network .
14. The method of claim 1 , further comprising providing
information concerning the presence or absence of said at
least five polynucleotide analytes to a health care profes
sional , wherein said health care professional makes a clinical
decision based on said information .
15. The method of claim 14 , wherein said clinical decision
is a treatment decision .
16. The method of claim 15 , wherein said treatment
decision comprises treatment with an antibiotic or an anti
cancer therapeutic .

( 57 ) ABSTRACT
This disclosure provides methods , systems , compositions , and kits for the multiplexed detection of a plurality of analytes in a sample . In some examples , this disclosure provides methods , systems , compositions , and kits wherein multiple analytes may be detected in a single sample volume by acquiring a cumulative measurement or measurements of at least one quantifiable component of a signal . In some cases , additional components of a signal , or additional signals ( or components thereof ) are also quantified . Each signal or component of a signal may be used to construct a coding scheme which can then be used to determine the presence or absence of any analyte .

Of course , as described else- 25 where in the specification , the initial assigned value can be greater than one , for example to better distinguish over noise . Similarly , the values assigned to each analyte can be greater than the cumulative intensity values for the prior analytes plus one , for example , to increase the separation 30 between the intensities and enable more simple assignment

What is claimed is :
1. A method of unambiguously detecting any unique 30
combination of presence or absence of at least five poly
nucleotide analytes in a plurality of droplets , the method
comprising :
( a ) providing a sample comprising , or potentially com
prising , at least one of said at least five polynucleotide 35
analytes ;
( b ) forming a mixture of said sample and at least five
hybridization probes , wherein each of said at least five
hybridization probes further comprises at least one
fluorophore and at most four fluorophores ; 40
( c ) partitioning said mixture into said plurality of droplets ;
( d ) exciting said at least one fluorophore to generate one
or more signals if one or more of said at least five
polynucleotide analytes is present in said plurality of
droplets , wherein said one or more signals comprise at 45
least one signal generated by excitement of said at least
one fluorophore ;
( e ) measuring said one or more signals to generate a
cumulative intensity measurement , wherein said cumu 50
lative intensity measurement corresponds to the pres
ence of a unique combination of presence or absence of
said at least five polynucleotide analytes in said sample ;
and
( f ) determining whether each of said least five polynucle- 55
otide analytes is present , in any unique combination of
presence or absence , based on said cumulative intensity
measurement ,
wherein the method does not require any step of
immobilization of said at least five polynucleotide 60
analytes or mass spectrometry .
2. The method of claim 1 , wherein each of said at least
five hybridization probes is complementary to one of said at
least five polynucleotide analytes .
3. The method of claim 1 , wherein said at least five 65
hybridization probes comprise one or more fluorophores
selected from one , two , three , or four fluorophores .
4. The method of claim 1 , wherein , in ( b ) , a droplet of said
plurality of droplets comprises said at least five hybridiza
tion probes .
5. The method of claim 1 , wherein , in ( b ) , a droplet of said
plurality of droplets comprises one or more of said at least
five polynucleotide analytes .
6. The method of claim 1 , wherein , in ( b ) , a droplet of said
plurality of droplets comprises at most one of said at least
five polynucleotide analytes .
7. The method of claim 1 , wherein said one or more
signals is generated during a polymerase chain reaction .
8. The method of claim 1 , wherein said at least five
polynucleotide analytes are at least seven polynucleotide
analytes .
9. The method of claim 1 , wherein said at least five
hybridization probes are at least seven hybridization probes .
10. The method of claim 1 , wherein said one or more of
said at least five polynucleotide analytes comprise cell - free
nucleic acid , tumor nucleic acid , fetal nucleic acid , viral
nucleic acid , or any combination thereof .
11. The method of claim 1 , wherein said sample is a
biological sample derived from a subject .
12. The method of claim 11 , wherein detecting the pres
ence or absence of said at least five polynucleotide analytes
indicates the presence of cancer or an infection with a
pathogen in said subject .
13. The method of claim 1 , further comprising transmit
ting information concerning the presence or absence of said
at least five polynucleotide analytes through a computer
network .
14. The method of claim 1 , further comprising providing
information concerning the presence or absence of said at
least five polynucleotide analytes to a health care profes
sional , wherein said health care professional makes a clinical
decision based on said information .
15. The method of claim 14 , wherein said clinical decision
is a treatment decision .
16. The method of claim 15 , wherein said treatment
decision comprises treatment with an antibiotic or an anti
cancer therapeutic .

3. Polymerase Chain Reactions 60 measurements were obtained in the following channels after

All PCR reactions were performed in a ROCHE 480
LIGHTCYCLER instrument. Forty-five thermal cycles were
performed, with a 60 second hot-start at 95° C. The cycling
conditions for denaturation, annealing, and extension were
45 seconds, 50 seconds, and 60 seconds at 95° C., 65° C.,
and 70° C., respectively. Each experiment was run in quin-
tuplicate, with a reaction volume of 15 wL. Fluorescence

65

every annealing step: 483 nm to 533 nm (FAM), 523 nm to
568 nm (Cy3), 558 nm to 610 nm (ROX), and 615 nm to 670
nm (Cy5). Fluorescence measurements were also obtained
after the hot-start and the end of the 45 thermal cycles. The
change in the fluorescence intensity between these two
measurements (after hot-start and at the end of the 45 cycles)
determined the end-point fluorescent signal.

Claim 1 is drawn to a method of detecting any unique combination of presence or
absence of at least five polynucleotides in a plurality of droplets. The method comprises
providing a sample potentially comprising at least one of the at least five polynucleotide
analytes. The method comprises forming a mixture of the sample and at least five
hybridization probes, each comprising a fluorophore selected from at most four
fluorophores. The method comprises partitioning the mixture into the plurality of
droplets. The method comprises exciting the fluorophores to generate signals of one or
more of the at least five polynucleotide analytes is present in said plurality of droplets.
The signals comprise at least one signal generated by excitement of the one or more
fluorophores. The method comprises measuring the signals to generate a cumulative
measurement. The cumulative measurement corresponds to the presence of a unique
combination of presence or absence of the at least five polynucleotide analytes in the
sample. The method does not require any step of immobilization of the at least five
polynucleotide analytes or mass spectrometry.
Claim 2 is further limiting wherein each of the at least five hybridization probes is
complementary to one of the at least five polynucleotide analytes.
Claims 3-6 and 8-9 provides further constraints on the numbers of analytes,
probes, and fluorophores.

The document of Han et al. studies quantum dot tagged microbeads for
Page 5

illustrates four different polynucleotide analytes labeled with four different combinations
of three different fluorophores. The bottom three polynucleotide analytes are hybridized
to complementary polynucleotide probes. When the sample undergo spectroscopy, the
optical code on the right panel of the figure is the cumulative measurement of the
combination of fluorophores for each of the four polynucleotide analytes. The technique
of Han et al. does not involve immobilization or mass spectrometry.
Han et al. does not teach a mixture of at least five hybridization analytes. Han et
al. does not teach partitioning the mixture into droplets or conducting PCR.
The document of Lin et al. teaches nucleic acid nanostructure barcode probes
[title]. The abstract of Lin et al. teaches that uniquely fluorescently labeled
polynucleotide analytes are used as barcode hybridization probes. Figure 2 of Lin et al.
illustrates histograms for a combinatorial number of probes having one of 27 different
barcodes.
Han et al. and Lin et al. do not teach partitioning the mixture into droplets or
conducting PCR.

section of Vogelstein et al. teaches diluting and partitioning a genome into many small
droplets on many 96 well plates such that anywhere between zero to one to all of the
polynucleotide analytes may be present in each droplet.

evidence.text:
Claims 1-12 and 20 is/are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being
unpatentable over Han et al. [Nature Biotechnology, volume 19, 2001, pages 631-635;
on IDS] in view of Lin et al. [WO 2012/058638 A2] in view of Vogelstein et al. [PNAS,
volume 96, 1999, pages 9236-9241 ].
Claim 1 is drawn to a method of detecting any unique combination of presence or
absence of at least five polynucleotides in a plurality of droplets. The method comprises
providing a sample potentially comprising at least one of the at least five polynucleotide
analytes. The method comprises forming a mixture of the sample and at least five
hybridization probes, each comprising a fluorophore selected from at most four
fluorophores. The method comprises partitioning the mixture into the plurality of
droplets. The method comprises exciting the fluorophores to generate signals of one or
more of the at least five polynucleotide analytes is present in said plurality of droplets.
The signals comprise at least one signal generated by excitement of the one or more
fluorophores. The method comprises measuring the signals to generate a cumulative
measurement. The cumulative measurement corresponds to the presence of a unique
combination of presence or absence of the at least five polynucleotide analytes in the
sample. The method does not require any step of immobilization of the at least five
polynucleotide analytes or mass spectrometry.
Claim 2 is further limiting wherein each of the at least five hybridization probes is
complementary to one of the at least five polynucleotide analytes.
Claims 3-6 and 8-9 provides further constraints on the numbers of analytes,
probes, and fluorophores.
BIO-RAD EX.1030.005

Application/Control Number: 15/914,356
Art Unit: 1631
Claim 7 is further limiting and requires PCR.
The document of Han et al. studies quantum dot tagged microbeads for
Page 5
multiplexed optical coding of biomolecules [title]. Figure 5 on page 634 of Han et al.
illustrates four different polynucleotide analytes labeled with four different combinations
of three different fluorophores. The bottom three polynucleotide analytes are hybridized
to complementary polynucleotide probes. When the sample undergo spectroscopy, the
optical code on the right panel of the figure is the cumulative measurement of the
combination of fluorophores for each of the four polynucleotide analytes. The technique
of Han et al. does not involve immobilization or mass spectrometry.
Han et al. does not teach a mixture of at least five hybridization analytes. Han et
al. does not teach partitioning the mixture into droplets or conducting PCR.
The document of Lin et al. teaches nucleic acid nanostructure barcode probes
[title]. The abstract of Lin et al. teaches that uniquely fluorescently labeled
polynucleotide analytes are used as barcode hybridization probes. Figure 2 of Lin et al.
illustrates histograms for a combinatorial number of probes having one of 27 different
barcodes.
Han et al. and Lin et al. do not teach partitioning the mixture into droplets or
conducting PCR.
The document of Vogelstein et al. studies digital PCR [title]. The methods
section of Vogelstein et al. teaches diluting and partitioning a genome into many small
droplets on many 96 well plates such that anywhere between zero to one to all of the
polynucleotide analytes may be present in each droplet.
BIO-RAD EX.1030.006

Application/Control Number: 15/914,356
Art Unit: 1631
Page 6
With regard to claim 10, the experiments in Han et al. are performed on DNA that
is cell-free.
With regard to claims 11-12, Figure 5 of Vogelstein et al. teaches performing
digital PCR on a stool sample of a subject to determine presence of cancer.
With regard to claim 20, the methods section of Vogelstein et al. teaches diluting
the mixtures of polynucleotide analytes into a fixed concentration in the mixture of the
plurality of droplets such that Figure 1 of Vogelstein et al. illustrates presence/absence
patterns of the polynucleotide analyzes in each of the droplet wells.
It would have been obvious to someone of ordinary skill in the art at the time of
the instant invention to modify the labeling of Han et al. by use of the labeling of Lin et
al. wherein the motivation would have been that the barcodes of Lin et al. generate a
combinatorial number of labels [Figure 2 of Lin et al.].
It would have been obvious to someone of ordinary skill in the art at the time of
the instant invention to modify the labeling of Han et al. and Lin et al. by use of the
digital PCR of Vogelstein wherein the motivation would have been that the partitioning
into droplets facilitates identifying presence/absence patterns of polynucleotide
analytes.
There would have been a reasonable expectation of success in combining Han
et al., Lin et al., and Vogelstein et al. because all three studies analogously pertain to
BIO-RAD EX.1030.007

Application/Control Number: 15/914,356
Art Unit: 1631
Page 7
fluorophore labeling of polynucleotide analytes to determine their presence/absence
patterns.
Response to arguments:
Applicant's arguments filed 23 May 2019 have been fully considered but they are
not persuasive.
Applicant reiterates the limitations of the claims (specifically cumulative
measurement) are argues, without support that Han et al. does not teach the limitations
of the claims. This argument is not persuasive for the reasons discussed in the
rejection statement above. In addition, the plots in Figure 5 of Han et al. represent
cumulative measurements of quantum dots colors within the microbead.
Applicant reiterates the limitations of the claims (specifically the lack of
immobilization) are argues, without support that neither Lin et al. nor Vogelstein et al.
does not teach the limitations of the claims. This argument is not persuasive for the
reasons discussed in the rejection statement above. In addition, Han et al. (and not Lin
et al. or Vogelstein et al.) is relied upon for the teaching of the exclusion of
immobilization and mass spectrometry.
The following rejection is reiterated:
35 U.S.C. 103 Rejection #2:
